S1.why: Class-10 concord za agrees with the unspoken cutling, so the label says 'the free five' in 9 characters.

S2.why: An invitation to carry on, using kuhifadhi, the ordinary Swahili verb for saving; no limit word such as kikomo.

S3.s: Umetumia cutling zote %lld za bure. Zitaendelea kuwa bure na kufanya kazi kama kawaida.
S3.back: You-have-used cutling all 5 of free. They-will-continue to-be free and to-do work as usual.
S3.why: Second-person singular as in the vocab; 'kama kawaida' (as usual) is how a speaker reassures that nothing changes.

S4.why: States the allowance plainly; numeral follows the noun, as in the vocab's 'Cutling %lld'.

S5.s: Umetumia cutling %lld kati ya %lld za bure.
S5.back: You-have-used cutling 3 among of 5 of free.
S5.why: 'X kati ya Y' is the native 'X of Y'; numbers keep English order, so no positional forms are needed.

S6.why: A noun phrase like a row heading; nafasi (room, space) is the word the grid after purchase shows.

S7.s: Hifadhi hadi cutling %@ za maandishi na %lld za picha.
S7.back: Save up-to cutling 5,000 of text and 500 of picture.
S7.why: Builds on the vocab's 'Cutling ya maandishi' and 'Cutling ya picha', so the two kinds keep their app names.

S8.why: Swahili lists with na before the last item and no comma before it.

S9.s: Ununuzi mmoja unatosha kila kifaa kilichoingia kwa Apple Account yako.
S9.back: Purchase one suffices every device that-has-signed-in with Apple Account your.
S9.why: Reuses the vocab's own phrase 'kila kifaa kilichoingia kwa Apple Account yako', so the account sentence reads the same across the app.

S10.why: 'Malipo ya mara moja' is the set phrase for a one-time payment; as a noun phrase it cannot be misread as 'pay immediately'.

S11.s: Hakuna usajili, matangazo wala kufungua akaunti.
S11.back: There-is-no subscription, advertisements nor to-open account.
S11.why: Usajili is the store word for subscription, so sign-up is said as kufungua akaunti to keep the two apart; wala is the native 'nor'.

S12.why: The wording Swahili store and app UIs use for restoring purchases; sentence case, as Swahili does not title-case.

S13.why: Present progressive -na- with the single ellipsis character.

S14.why: Kufungua is the Swahili unlock; 'mara moja' is left out of the button because there it also reads 'right away', and S10 directly above already says one-time.

S15.why: Same command without the price, exactly 14 characters.

S16.why: The everyday way to put something off without refusing it.

S17.why: The plain verb Swahili interfaces use on close buttons.

S18.why: Short, warm and a little proud; 'yote' (all of it) takes in the room the grid shows.

S19.s: Asante kwa kununua. Hii inasaidia Cutling na mtu pekee anayeitengeneza.
S19.back: Thanks for buying. This helps Cutling and person sole who-makes-it.
S19.why: 'Mtu pekee' (the only person) says one maker without the vagueness of 'mtu mmoja' (a certain person).

S20.s: Karibu tena. Ununuzi wako wa awali umerejeshwa.
S20.back: Welcome again. Purchase your of before has-been-restored.
S20.why: 'Karibu tena' is how a returning person is greeted; the verb matches S12 and S13 (rejesha).

S21.s: %lld kati ya cutling %lld za bure zimetumika
S21.back: 3 among of cutling 5 of free have-been-used
S21.why: Describes the tile row for VoiceOver; zimetumika agrees with cutling in class 10.

S22.s: Una cutling %lld. Sasa kuna nafasi ya cutling %@.
S22.back: You-have cutling 5. Now there-is room of cutling 5,000.
S22.why: The numeral as a digit after an invariant noun takes no agreement, so it reads correctly for 1, 2, 5 and 21.

S23.s: Cutling imefunguliwa. Sasa kuna nafasi ya cutling %@.
S23.back: Cutling has-been-unlocked. Now there-is room of cutling 5,000.
S23.why: Class-9 subject prefix i- for the app name, and the same room phrase as S22.

S24.why: Names what happened with the purchase as subject, so nobody is blamed.

S25.s: App Store haipatikani kwa sasa. Jaribu tena baadaye kidogo.
S25.back: App Store is-not-reachable for now. Try again later a-little.
S25.why: 'Baadaye kidogo' is the spoken 'in a bit'; the store name stays in English as Swahili users see it.

S26.why: One factual sentence with the store as subject.

S27.s: Apple Account ya kifaa hiki haina ununuzi wa awali wa Cutling.
S27.back: Apple Account of device this has-no purchase of before of Cutling.
S27.why: Puts the account first so the sentence is short and says where the search happened.

S28.s: Toleo la bure linahifadhi cutling %lld. Ukifungua Cutling mara moja tu, utahifadhi kadri upendavyo.
S28.back: Version of free keeps cutling 5. If-you-unlock Cutling time one only, you-will-save as-much-as you-like.
S28.why: Conditional uki- carries 'once you unlock'; 'mara moja tu' (just once) cannot be read as 'right away' with tu; 'kadri upendavyo' is the native 'as many as you like'.

S29.why: Same 'kati ya' pair as S5; 19 characters, one over the 18 budget, because 'za bure' is the shortest way to say free here.

K1.s: Nafasi %lld za bure zimejaa. Gusa ufungue
K1.back: Slots 5 of free are-full. Tap you-unlock
K1.why: 38 characters; nafasi (slots) as in S6, and 'gusa ufungue' (tap so you unlock) is a natural spoken command.

M1.why: Kamili is added on the Mac because in the Window menu 'Fungua Cutling' alone could read 'Open Cutling'.

M2.why: The same command as M1 with the ellipsis character, as it opens a window.

M3.why: Row label with the item word and class-10 za.

M4.why: A compact pair, since 'kati ya' would take 11 characters against a budget of 10.

M5.why: The same status words as S23.

M6.s: Ununuzi mmoja unafungua Cutling kwenye iPhone, iPad na Mac.
M6.back: Purchase one unlocks Cutling on iPhone, iPad and Mac.

M7.s: Imefunguliwa kwenye iPhone, iPad na Mac kwa Apple Account hii.
M7.back: Has-been-unlocked on iPhone, iPad and Mac with Apple Account this.
M7.why: 'Kwa Apple Account' follows the vocab's preposition for the account.

M8.s: Ulinunua Cutling kabla haijawa bure, kwa hiyo itabaki imefunguliwa. Asante sana.
M8.back: You-bought Cutling before it-had-not-become free, so it-will-remain unlocked. Thanks much.
M8.why: 'Kabla' with the negative perfect is the native 'before it became'; 'asante sana' is the plain warm thanks.
